sections.history: Thiruvali and Thirunagari are two neighbouring villages near Sirkazhi, in the Mayiladuthurai country, and their two temples are counted together as a single Divya Desam — one of the 108 abodes of Vishnu sung by the Alvar saints in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham — in Chola Nadu. Thirumangai Alvar praised the pair together, in 41 pasurams. Thirunagari is held to be his home country, and tradition says that his consort Kumudavalli was raised there. At Thiruvali the presiding lord is Azhagiyasingar, Lakshmi Narasimha, with the Goddess as Poornavalli, also named Amruthagadavalli. At Thirunagari stands the Vedarajan temple, whose festival image is Kalyana Ranganathar. Its antiquity is carried by the Alvar's hymns.
sections.architecture: The Thiruvali temple is a Dravidian shrine of the Chola country, with the Ilakshmi Pushkarini as its tank. Its sanctum is unusual among Narasimha temples: the Goddess Lakshmi is seated on the lord's right side. A south-facing shrine of Thirumangai Alvar stands outside the temple walls. At Thirunagari, the Vedarajan temple has its own shrine of the Alvar, facing north, in a raised enclosure.
sections.legends: Tradition tells that Narasimha appeared to Thirumangai Alvar at Thiruvali, and the shrine remembers that meeting. A second legend binds the two temples: Lakshmi is said to have left Vaikuntha and hidden herself in a lotus bud in the tank at Thirunagari. The two villages are thus held to be one story told in two places. Tradition also remembers Thirunagari as the place where Kumudavalli, the Alvar's consort, grew up.
sections.festivals: The most prominent festival is the Thirumangai Alvar Utsavam in the month of Thai (January–February), when the Alvar is honoured at both temples. A Garuda Sevai is also observed in January. The temples keep four daily rituals and three yearly festivals.
sections.experience: Plan to visit both temples, close together, since they are one Divya Desam. At Thiruvali look for Lakshmi seated beside Narasimha; at Thirunagari seek out the Alvar's shrine and the Vedarajan sanctum. The visit pairs well with the nearby Sirkazhi temples.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan sessions and a midday closure; confirm current timings locally before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: Thiruvali and Thirunagari lie close together near Sirkazhi in Mayiladuthurai district, reached by road from Sirkazhi. Sirkazhi, on the Chennai–Mayiladuthurai rail line, is the nearest station; the nearest major airport is Tiruchirappalli, about 160 km away.
